state.objective: Decide the remaining Finance navigation ambiguities using concrete frequency, authorization and task-completion facts rather than abstract labels.

users_and_frequency.AP_staff: Daily: validate invoices, matching, aging, prepare payment candidates. Cannot release bank payments or approve own exceptions.
users_and_frequency.Treasury_staff: Daily: payment instructions, bank release after approval, statements, bank reconciliation preparation. Cannot approve own release or final reconciliation.
users_and_frequency.General_Accounting: Daily/periodic: ledger investigation, controlled manual journals, posting-rule exceptions, asset accounting and close preparation.
users_and_frequency.Finance_Manager: Approvals, exceptions, reports and close oversight.
users_and_frequency.Auditor: Occasional read-only inspection of the same records, evidence, approvals and logs.
users_and_frequency.Unit_user: Uses Operations/Store for physical cash and evidence; has no company-bank or manual-GL authority.

screen_facts: Cash & bank is one workspace row with tabs. Bank Accounts is restricted, changed infrequently and used as context for statements and reconciliation.
Charges without a sale arise from bank/acquirer lines and are worked as reconciliation exceptions; Overview can show their count.
System entries are visible through Ledger. Manual journal creation is rare, restricted, reason-coded, approved and audited; accountants still need a queue/history of drafts, approvals and reversals.

Reports holds financial statements and aging. Ledger holds searchable posted entries by account/dimension/document. Trial Balance is a summarized debit-credit balance for a period and is used in close/report review.
Financing contains bank-loan schedules plus owner capital/drawings. It is restricted and periodic, but these records drive current/noncurrent classification, interest, repayments and disclosures.

Role filtering can show AP 5-7 relevant rows, Treasury 4-6, General Accounting 7-10, Manager 8-11 and Auditor read-only 8-11. The union of all Finance capabilities may have 13 rows, but no ordinary specialist must see all of them.
Server permissions enforce every mutation; hiding a row is only a usability choice.

The agreed strong decisions already reduce the union menu to: Overview, Accounts payable, Payments, Cash & bank, Asset accounting, Manual journals, Reports, Ledger, Tax, Financing, Period close, Chart of accounts, Posting rules.

union_13_role_filtered.instructions: Is a 13-row union acceptable when ordinary specialists see only their authorized 4-10 rows and groups remain Work, Books, Controls and Setup?

criteria.yes: Judge the menu each role actually sees, not the union of all capabilities.
criteria.no: The union itself must be reduced even if roles never see it all.

bank_account_tab.instructions: Given that bank accounts are infrequently maintained and directly contextualize statements and reconciliation, should Bank Accounts be a restricted tab/settings view within Cash & bank?

criteria.yes: Keep the work and its master context in one workspace.
criteria.no: Use a separate persistent sidebar destination.

unmatched_exception.instructions: Given that charges without a sale originate from statement/acquirer lines and are reconciliation exceptions, should they be an exception tab in Cash & bank plus an Overview alert?

criteria.yes: They are a filtered work queue in the same reconciliation domain.
criteria.no: They are an independent accounting domain requiring a top-level row.

manual_journal_destination.instructions: Given the need to find draft, pending-approval, posted, reversed and rejected manual journals, should authorized General Accounting have a persistent Manual journals destination?

criteria.yes: A controlled document lifecycle requires its own queue/history screen.
criteria.no: A create action inside Ledger is sufficient for the entire lifecycle.

reports_ledger_jobs.instructions: Given that Reports answers financial-position/performance questions while Ledger investigates individual postings and documents, should they remain separate destinations?

criteria.yes: They are distinct recurring jobs with different filters and outputs.
criteria.no: One screen should combine both jobs.

trial_balance_report_tab.instructions: Given that Trial Balance is a summarized period balance used in close and report review, should it be a Reports tab while Ledger opens detailed postings?

criteria.yes: Summary belongs with period reports and can drill into Ledger.
criteria.no: Ledger should open on Trial Balance before any account is selected.

financing_persistent.instructions: Given that loans and owner equity have schedules, classifications, interest/repayment events and disclosures, should assigned Finance roles have a Financing destination?

criteria.yes: Keep a restricted persistent workspace for the controlled lifecycle.
criteria.no: Use only generic Payments and Manual journals with no financing register.

auditor_same_information_architecture.instructions: Given that auditors inspect the same records, evidence, approval history and logs without mutation rights, should they use the same information architecture in read-only mode?

criteria.yes: Reuse the same screens with read-only controls and audit filters.
criteria.no: Maintain a separate auditor-only navigation tree and screens.

specialist_row_target.instructions: Which target best balances findability and cognitive load for a normal AP, Treasury, Tax or Accounting specialist after role filtering?

criteria.four_to_seven: 4-7 persistent rows for narrow specialists; managers/accounting may see more.
criteria.eleven_to_thirteen: Every Finance role should see nearly the full union.

manager_row_target.instructions: How many rows should a Finance Manager normally see for oversight and approval?

criteria.seven_to_nine: 7-9 rows, with less frequent setup reached from relevant workspaces.
criteria.ten_to_thirteen: 10-13 rows including all controls and restricted setup.
